browser-phase5-pair-once.title: Pair-once: stop re-pairing every cold session
browser-phase5-pair-once.description: Every fresh ClosePaw process re-runs the full TLS-PSK SPAKE2 pair handshake even though the RSA keypair persists under filesDir/adb_self_pair/ and adbd already has the pubkey in /data/misc/adb/adb_keys. Cost: ~1s extra latency + one extra adb_keys entry per cold session. Root cause: AdbWirelessManager.isPubkeyAuthorized(fingerprint) always returns false because the fingerprint formats do not line up — we hash the X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER but adbd hashes a different byte sequence. Fix sketch: change AdbCryptoKeyStore.fingerprint() to return SHA-256(AndroidPubkey.encode(pubkey)) — the 524-byte adbd-format input — or have it return the raw base64-encoded AndroidPubkey blob; change AdbWirelessManager.isPubkeyAuthorized to take that base64 string and substring-match against adb_keys content (read via shell-uid binder). See handoff outstanding item #1.
acceptCriteria: AdbWirelessManager.isPubkeyAuthorized returns true on second cold session when adb_keys still contains our pubkey

browser-phase5-emulator-regression.title: Restore emulator-5554 and re-verify Phase 4 path
browser-phase5-emulator-regression.description:
emulator-5554 went offline mid-debug after `setprop persist.adb.tls.trace 1; stop adbd; start adbd`. `adb reconnect` does not recover. Agent drives this end-to-end:
1. Check `adb devices` — if emulator-5554 still offline, kill it (`adb -s emulator-5554 emu kill` may fail; otherwise `pkill -f qemu-system.*-5554`) and restart via `~/android-sdk/emulator/emulator @<avd> -no-snapshot &`. List AVDs with `~/android-sdk/emulator/emulator -list-avds`.
2. Alternative: emulator-5556 is already running and available. If restarting -5554 is flaky, target -5556 instead — task acceptCriteria say `emulator` not specifically -5554.
3. Once emulator shows `device`, ensure Wi-Fi connected: `adb -s <emu> shell cmd wifi connect-network AndroidWifi open` (synthetic AndroidWifi; BSSID 02:15:b2:00:01:00).
4. Run wireless self-pair flow: `ANDROID_SERIAL=<emu> DEBUG_AUTO_APPROVE=true ./scripts/debug-run.sh "Use browser_script to fetch document.title from open https://example.com"`
5. Verify logcat shows `WirelessAdbSelfPair: wireless-adb pairing complete` and agent answers `document.title is "Example Domain"`.
6. Append PASS row to projects/active/browser/real_device_qa.md with debug-output run dir.

browser-phase5-delete-dead-transports.title: Delete dead transports (APP_PROCESS, HOST_MEDIATED_RELAY, CHROME_TCP_LOOPBACK)
browser-phase5-delete-dead-transports.description:
Three transports add cost and noise but no value:
(a) APP_PROCESS (AppProcessLocalSocketTransport) — never works on stock Android. Untrusted_app cannot connectto another apps abstract socket (no TE allow rule + MLS category mismatch). No phase of QA observed it succeed.
(b) HOST_MEDIATED_RELAY (HostMediatedCdpRelayTransport) — needs PC-side `adb forward`/`reverse`, contradicts in-device autonomy. Was the only working path on locked OEMs before Phase 4; superseded.
(c) CHROME_TCP_LOOPBACK (ChromeRemoteDebugPortTransport, the Phase 2 attempt) — empirically blocked by chromes per-profile flag requirement, kept `wired but null in production`.

After deletion the cascade collapses to APP_PROCESS-removed → USER_SERVICE → WIRELESS_ADB_SELF_PAIR. Bridge constructor: 4 transport slots → 1. httpGet cascade: ~80 → ~25 lines. DevtoolsSetupError: 9 sealed subtypes → 4-5. See handoff outstanding item #7 + the Phase 2 sub-bullet of item #8.

browser-phase5-bridge-simplify.title: Simplify ShizukuChromeDevtoolsBridge: cascade, error block, defensive sleeps
browser-phase5-bridge-simplify.description:
Once dead transports are deleted (browser-phase5-delete-dead-transports) and pair-once lands (browser-phase5-pair-once), the bridge should collapse to a clean shape. Specific things to clean:
- Cascade in httpGet collapses to APP_PROCESS-removed → user → wireless; error logic becomes `first DevtoolsSetupError wins, otherwise WirelessAdbSelfPairUnavailable`. End-block error-priority logic touching appError/userError/wirelessError/relayUnreachable goes away.
- DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS bumped 4_000 → 30_000 because chromes /json/version did not EOF — with readUntilHttpComplete this is no longer needed; restore 4s default and let script-level timeout cap the outer budget.
- POST_CNXN_SETTLE_MS (200ms) and POST_PAIR_SETTLE_MS (500ms) defensive sleeps added during debug — re-evaluate; if still needed, document why; if not, delete.
- WirelessAdbSelfPairTransport.exchange outer try/catch with Log.e re-throw was added because the bridges runCatching swallowed exceptions. Re-evaluate after cascade simplifies.
- WirelessAdbSelfPairTransport.isReachable() does a currentBssid() shell-out via Shizuku binder during preflight. Collapse to a single check after cascade simplifies.
- AdbWirelessManager.isPubkeyAuthorized — delete if not fixed by browser-phase5-pair-once; ensure consistency.
- UserServiceTransport.binder made public in commit ec4d2e92. Either keep with named accessor + WHY comment or refactor AdbWirelessManager to take the same UserServiceProvider the bridge uses.
- Comments + docs: keep load-bearing AOSP-line-number comments; prune narration. Per CLAUDE.md `Default to writing no comments`.
- Tests: AdbWireProtocolClientTests in-process FakeAdbd already mirrors post-mTLS contract — add coverage for readUntilHttpComplete: Content-Length response, no-Content-Length response, A_CLSE before headers complete, A_CLSE after partial body.

See handoff outstanding item #8.

browser-phase5-adb-keys-cleanup.title: adb_keys cleanup utility (unpair helper)
browser-phase5-adb-keys-cleanup.description: Until pair-once lands, /data/misc/adb/adb_keys accumulates one entry per cold session. There is no built-in cleanup. Eventually adbds iteration over the file becomes O(N) per handshake. Not urgent but worth adding a disablePairing + unpairDevice helper that prunes our old entries. Becomes much smaller once browser-phase5-pair-once lands (no new entries per run), but a one-time cleanup of accumulated entries is still useful. See handoff outstanding item #4.

browser-phase5-qa-mid.title: Mid-cleanup regression gate (post delete + pair-once)
browser-phase5-qa-mid.description:
Mid-cleanup regression gate. Agent drives nubia P0110 (`100.64.43.95:5555`) end-to-end after the two upstream tasks land + merge to main:
1. After orchestrator merges browser-phase5-pair-once + browser-phase5-delete-dead-transports to main, this task runs from main HEAD.
2. Setup: `./scripts/setup.sh` to install fresh APK + start Shizuku.
3. Force fresh pair: `adb -s 100.64.43.95:5555 shell run-as ai.closepaw rm -rf files/adb_self_pair`
4. Strip host plumbing: `adb -s 100.64.43.95:5555 forward --remove-all && adb -s 100.64.43.95:5555 reverse --remove-all`
5. Cold session 1: `ANDROID_SERIAL=100.64.43.95:5555 DEBUG_AUTO_APPROVE=true ./scripts/debug-run.sh "Use browser_script to fetch document.title from open https://example.com"` — capture logcat from this run.
6. Cold session 2 (no rm -rf this time): same command. Verify logcat now shows `wireless-adb pair skipped: pubkey already authorized` (the pair-once observable).
7. Verify adb_keys not growing: `adb -s 100.64.43.95:5555 shell wc -l /data/misc/adb/adb_keys` before and after session 2 returns the same count.
8. Verify deleted transport labels absent: `grep -E `APP_PROCESS|HOST_MEDIATED_RELAY|CHROME_TCP_LOOPBACK` <session-2-logcat>` returns no hits.
9. Append PASS row to real_device_qa.md.
